items.label: text
items.text: We are going to use ideas from Topic 12 on entropy and apply themto equilibriumsituations.

items.label: list_item
items.text: In Topic 12,we introduced the equation for calculating the total entropy change:

items.label: formula
items.text: ΔS_total = ΔS_system + ΔS_surroundings

items.label: text
items.text: We also stated thatStotal is positivefor all spontaneous changes.

items.label: text
items.text: There is very little change in Ssystem with a change in temperature, unlessthereisachangeinstateofoneofthereactantsor products. However, there are significant changes to △Ssurroundings

items.label: text
items.text: The entropy change of the surroundings during a chemical reaction isgiven by:

items.label: formula
items.text: ΔS_surroundings = − ΔH / T

items.label: text
items.text: where △His the enthalpy change and T is the absolute temperature(i.e.the temperature measured in kelvin).

items.text: Wecanusethisinformationtofindoutifareactionis spontaneousataparticulartemperature.
